lines.trans: What a lovely garden green! Give me a brush—the owner must help too!
Boss, you are wearing a snow-white shirt and polished black shoes.
Just three neat slats on the bottom! I have a steady hand, watch!
Careful, Mazen, your sleeve is two centimetres from the wet edge—
Missed my shirt completely! Ha! Wait... my nose itches.
Mazen, don't lift the hand holding the green brush—!
Why are you both staring at my forehead like that?
Because you just painted the left lens of your reading glasses bright green.
My glasses were on my forehead again?! Oh, everything looks like a forest!
Stand completely still! Warm water and a soft cloth—off it comes!
Clean as new! Thank you, Nour... I think I will go supervise the front desk.
Wise decision, boss. Leave the wet paint to us.

See you soon!

meanings.note: Reinforces negation ('not at all, never'): ما في زبدة أبدا ('no butter at all'), لا تقلق أبدا ('do not worry at all').

examples.trans: There is no butter in the fridge at all!
Do not worry at all, sir.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Primary colour adjective ('black'); feminine and non-human plural form is سودا (sooda).

examples.text: جيب لفة لزاق أسود من الدكان.
examples.trans: Pick up a roll of black tape from the shop.
The black cat is sleeping under the tree.

meanings.note: Form IV verb paired with على ('supervise / oversee a task').

examples.text: سلمى بتشرف عالمطبخ وهي قاعدة عالكرسي.
examples.trans: Salma supervises the kitchen while sitting in her chair.

examples.text: أبو طارق أشرف على تركيب الشيش الأخضر.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq oversaw the installation of the green shutters.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أنوف.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your nose now.
The air feels cold on my nose in the morning.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one man.

examples.trans: Did you plant these herbs yourself?
Did you plan this entire meeting?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببين, بيبين).

examples.text: لما بدهم يبينوا هاديين بيتأخروا دقيقتين.
examples.trans: When they want to play it cool, they arrive two minutes late.
The truth came out at the end of the week.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: Core Levantine verb for 'look (at)' taking على or في.

examples.text: تطلعي من الشباك شوفي لون الشيش الأخضر!
examples.trans: Look out the window and see the green colour of the shutters!

examples.text: ليش بتطلعوا علي هيك؟ هلا بمسح الدهان!
examples.trans: Why are you staring at me like that? I'll wipe the paint right now!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تلوج.

examples.trans: The water is cold as ice.
Snow fell on the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: Adverb 'exact, completely, perfectly'.

examples.trans: Its size fits you perfectly.
The street is completely empty at noon.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'two' (إنتو التنين 'the two of you'); note homograph التنين ('Monday').

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجبنة.

examples.trans: Your glasses are pushed up on your forehead!
He wiped the rain off his forehead.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحذية.

examples.trans: Take off your shoes by the door.
Inside the bag are two pairs of men's shoes.

meanings.note: Geminate verb meaning both 'itch' (أنفي بيحكني 'my nose itches') and 'scratch/rub'.

examples.text: استنوا لحظة، أنفي بيحكني وإيدي فيها دهان!
examples.trans: Wait a second—my nose itches and my hand has paint on it!

examples.text: مازن حك جبينه بطرف الفرشاية بالغلط.
examples.trans: Mazen scratched his forehead with the tip of the brush by mistake.

meanings.note: Describes a wise person or a smart, prudent choice (قرار حكيم).

examples.text: الراحة الليلة قرار حكيم عشان تطيب رجلك.
examples.trans: Resting tonight is a wise decision so your foot heals.

examples.text: أبو طارق معروف بالحارة برأيه الهادئ والحكيم.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq is known down the lane for his calm, wise advice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافية, plural: دافيين).

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

راح.gloss: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)

meanings.en: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بروح, بيروح).

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Describes wet fresh paint, damp morning stone, or moist cake.

examples.text: انتبه، طرف اللوح لسا رطب من الدهان!
examples.trans: Careful—the edge of the board is still wet with paint!

examples.text: مسحنا الطاولة بقماشة رطبة قبل ما نحط الفناجين.
examples.trans: We wiped the table with a damp cloth before setting down the cups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برفع, بيرفع).

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Spoken word for 'like': زيك 'like you'; زي ما 'just as, the way that'.

examples.trans: I want a glass of tea like yesterday.
Do it the way I taught you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: Shortened in speech to سنتي (dual سنتيين 'two centimetres').

examples.text: قيس المسافة بالمسطرة، لازم تكون عشرة سنتي.
examples.trans: Measure the gap with the ruler—it has to be ten centimetres.

examples.text: كم قميصك بعيد سنتيين بس عن الدهان الرطب!
examples.trans: Your shirt sleeve is only two centimetres from the wet paint!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Names both wooden shutter slats/louvres and thin slices of bread or lemon.

examples.text: دهنا شرائح الشيش الخشب وحدة ورا التانية.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden shutter slats one after another.

examples.text: حطينا شريحة ليمون رقيقة بجانب كاسة الشاي.
examples.trans: We placed a thin slice of lemon beside the tea glass.

meanings.note: Standard everyday 'thank you' across the Arabic-speaking world.

examples.trans: Thank you all very much!
Thank you for your patience, sir.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Hollow verb meaning 'hit the mark / splash onto / happen to someone'.

examples.text: الحمد لله الدهان الأخضر ما صاب قميصي.
examples.trans: Thankfully the green paint didn't touch my shirt.

examples.text: ولا نقطة مطر صابت الخشب الجديد بالممر.
examples.trans: Not a single drop of rain hit the new wood in the hallway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صحاب.

examples.trans: Who is the owner of the blue suitcase?
We became friends from the first day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أطراف.

examples.trans: Pull the edge of the sheet tight.

examples.text: حط الكاسة بعيد عن طرف الطاولة.
examples.trans: Set the glass away from the edge of the table.

meanings.note: Geminate verb; أظن / بظن means 'I think / I reckon'.

examples.text: أظن رح يضل عنا دهان كفاية للوحة البوابة.
examples.trans: I think we'll have enough paint left over for the gate sign.

examples.text: ظنيت إن السكر بالمرتبان الكبير مش الصغير.
examples.trans: I thought the sugar was in the big jar, not the small one.

meanings.note: Optical lens of eyeglasses or a camera (named after its lentil shape, عدس).

examples.text: مسحت العدسة اليسار من نظارتي بقماشة نضيفة.
examples.trans: I wiped the left lens of my glasses with a clean cloth.

examples.text: نقطة صغيرة عالعدسة بتخلي القراءة صعبة.
examples.trans: A tiny speck on the lens makes reading difficult.

meanings.note: Used in أخضر غابة / أخضر متل الغابة ('forest green') as well as pine/oak woods like Ajloun.

examples.text: اخترنا للشيش لون أخضر غامق متل الغابة.
examples.trans: We chose a deep forest-green colour for the shutters.

examples.text: غابات عجلون بتضل خضرا وحلوة طول السنة.
examples.trans: The forests of Ajloun stay green and lovely all year round.

meanings.note: Idiomatic Arabic colour modifier (أصفر فاقع 'bright lemon yellow', أخضر فاقع 'vivid green').

examples.text: لون الليمون الأصفر الفاقع طالع حلو جنب الأخضر.
examples.trans: The bright lemon-yellow colour looks great next to the green.

examples.text: ما بدنا لون فاقع، بدنا أخضر هادي متل الغابة.
examples.trans: We don't want a flashy shade—we want a calm forest green.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a paintbrush, hairbrush, or pastry brush.

examples.text: غسلنا الفرشايات بمي دافية أول ما خلصنا دهان.
examples.trans: We washed the brushes in warm water right after finishing the painting.

examples.text: لا ترفع الإيد اللي ماسكة الفرشاية الخضرا!
examples.trans: Don't lift the hand that's holding the green paintbrush!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قراءات.

examples.trans: We put a brass reading lamp by the desk.
I love reading in the quiet courtyard.

meanings.note: Standard and spoken noun for a choice or resolution (قرار حكيم 'a wise decision').

examples.text: تغيير الملصقات الليلة كان قرار حكيم بجد.
examples.trans: Replacing the labels tonight was truly a wise decision.

examples.text: أخدنا قرار نفتح الكافيه يوم الأربعا الصبح.
examples.trans: We made the decision to open the café on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Singulative of قماش ('fabric'); names a wiping or polishing cloth.

examples.text: جيب شوية مي دافية وقماشة نضيفة لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Bring a little warm water and a clean cloth, please.

examples.text: نشف الخشب بقماشة قطن قبل ما تدهن.
examples.trans: Wipe the wood dry with a cotton cloth before you paint.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قمصان.

examples.trans: He put on a neat, ironed white shirt.
He changed his shirt twice before the appointment.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Vocalized lemma distinguishing 'sleeve' (kumm, pl. kmaam كمام) from كم ('how many?').

examples.text: شمرت عن كمامي قبل ما نغسل الشبابيك.
examples.trans: I rolled up my sleeves before we washed the windows.

examples.text: تبللت كمام قميصي لما ركضنا تحت المطر.
examples.trans: My shirt sleeves got soaked when we ran in the rain.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلبس, بيلبس).

examples.text: أنا أكيد ما بلبس مقاس أربعة وأربعين!
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear size forty-four!

examples.text: لبس معطفه قبل ما يطلع بالمطر.
examples.trans: He put on his coat before going out in the rain.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'why?'.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مرتبة, plural: مرتبين).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting right away.
Neat pencil sketches.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسك, بيمسك).

examples.trans: Hold this torch steady right here.
Grab the boxes, Tariq!

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مكاتب.

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: Passive participle of لمّع ('to polish shoes, brass, or wood').

examples.text: مازن إجا بقميص أبيض مكوي وحذاء أسود ملمع.
examples.trans: Mazen arrived in a pressed white shirt and polished black shoes.

examples.text: الطاولات الخشب الملمعة بتعكس ضو الفوانيس.
examples.trans: The polished wooden tables reflect the glow of the lanterns.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناعمة, plural: ناعمين).

examples.trans: I brought two soft pillows for the attic.
Lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar.

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Lively conversational exclamation of triumph or attention ('ha! / there!').

examples.text: ما صاب قميصي ولا نقطة دهان، ها!
examples.trans: Not a single drop of paint touched my shirt—ha!

examples.text: ها، شو رأيكم باللون الأخضر تحت الشمس؟
examples.trans: Well, what do you think of the green colour in the sunshine?

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

هيك.gloss: like this; so (عشان هيك that's why)

meanings.en: like this; so (عشان هيك that's why)
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine word for 'like this / that way' (عشان هيك 'that is why', مع هيك 'even so').

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
And after that, where do I go?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!
